level1.text: Cobalt-60 emits gamma radiation, for whose mean energy $1.25\,\text{MeV}$ the half-value thickness of lead is $10.4\,\text{mm}$. What percentage of the gamma radiation passes through a lead plate with a thickness of $25.0\,\text{mm}$? Assume a narrow beam.

The kinetic energy of the alpha particle from the americium-241 source of a smoke detector is $5.49\,\text{MeV}$. In air, forming one ion pair takes on average $34\,\text{eV}$. How many ion pairs does the alpha particle form in air before it stops? Give the answer in the unit $10^{5}$.

Plates are added between a gamma source and a GM tube. When the plates have a total thickness of $18\,\text{mm}$, the net pulse count, that is the pulse count remaining after the background radiation, has decreased to an eighth of what it was without plates. What is the half-value thickness of the material of the plates for this gamma radiation? Give the answer in millimetres.

The spent fuel of a nuclear power plant is first stored in a water pool. The half-value thickness of water for a certain gamma radiation is $8.1\,\text{cm}$. What percentage of this gamma radiation passes through a $30\,\text{cm}$ layer of water? Assume a narrow beam.
At least $12.6\,\text{eV}$ is needed to ionise a water molecule. What is the longest wavelength at which a single photon can ionise a water molecule? Give the answer in nanometres.

level2.text: A GM counter counts $1260$ pulses in $3.00$ minutes near a radiation source. When the source is taken away, the counter counts $72$ pulses of background radiation in the same time. How many pulses per second does the radiation of the source cause? Give the answer in the unit $\tfrac{1}{\text{s}}$.

The gamma radiation of a caesium-137 source passes first through a $10\,\text{mm}$ lead plate and then through a $20\,\text{cm}$ concrete wall. The half-value thickness of lead is $5.5\,\text{mm}$ and that of concrete $3.9\,\text{cm}$. What percentage of the gamma radiation passes through both? Assume a narrow beam.

A student measures the radiation of a gamma source with a GM counter in periods of $10\,\text{s}$. Without a barrier the counter counts $480$ pulses and behind a $12\,\text{mm}$ layer of lead $105$ pulses. Without the source the counter counts $5$ pulses of background radiation in the same time. Based on the measurements, what is the half-value thickness of lead for this gamma radiation? Give the answer in millimetres.

A shield is designed around a radiation source. The half-value thickness for the gamma radiation of the source is $5.5\,\text{mm}$ for lead and $39\,\text{mm}$ for concrete. How thick a concrete wall attenuates the radiation as much as $10\,\text{mm}$ of lead? Give the answer in millimetres.

level3.text: An alpha particle of americium-241 with a kinetic energy of $5.49\,\text{MeV}$ stops in air after a distance of $4.1\,\text{cm}$. A beta particle with a kinetic energy of $1.0\,\text{MeV}$ travels in a winding path in air for about $3.6\,\text{m}$ before it stops. Both give up all their energy by ionising, and in air one ion pair takes on average $34\,\text{eV}$. How many times more ion pairs per centimetre does the alpha particle form than the beta particle? Assume that ion pairs are formed evenly along the whole track.

In a laboratory a GM counter shows $2400$ pulses per minute near a gamma source. When $11.0\,\text{mm}$ of lead is placed in front of the source, the reading is $630$ pulses per minute. The background radiation is $30$ pulses per minute. How thick a lead shield is needed for the pulse rate caused by the radiation of the source to drop to the same as the background radiation, $30$ pulses per minute? Give the answer in millimetres.

A WLAN network and a microwave oven use electromagnetic radiation with a frequency of $2.45\,\text{GHz}$. The ionisation energy of a water molecule is $12.6\,\text{eV}$. How many times greater is the ionisation energy than the energy of one photon of this radiation? Give the answer in the unit $10^{6}$.
